question_frozen_quote: froze: 'The title asks "are you living in a simulation?", but the abstract makes the real target narrower: must at least one of three propositions be true — (1) almost no civilizations reach a posthuman stage, (2) almost none that do run ancestor-simulations, (3) we are almost certainly in one?' | handed in: 'the explanation this document gives of why at least one of the three propositions must be true'
layer_at_fault_line: No finding here is contradicted by the document — the fixed/held/held-if/idle marks and the drop-a-condition, swap, catch-all-with-no-gauge and rival tests all check against Bostrom's own text; nothing to fault.
quotes: test_pull's two sides are not report part-list labels (P1-P5), so pairs_that_pull is empty though test_pull is RAN: 'by construction, f_P, f_I and N_I cannot all sit at "moderate" values simultaneously once N_I is huge — if you push f_P and f_I both away from zero, f_sim is pulled to near 1. This mutual pull *is* the engine of the whole argument, and it is math, not evidence, that holds it.' | test_poke has only one half named (a change said not to alter the outcome; no change is named that the report says WOULD alter it): 'Swap 10^21 or 10^42 ops/sec for numbers three orders of magnitude smaller: the conclusion is untouched, because the argument only needs N_I "extremely large," not any particular figure.' | test_reverse names a one-way direction without poking cause and effect separately: 'it matters for P5, where "no anomaly observed" could always be explained backward as simulator repair rather than as evidence against (3) — a one-way street that makes that particular claim untestable, not the paper's main result.' | P5's mark cell mixes a genuine mark with a non-mark description and is read as the single mark 'idle', since 'catch-all with no gauge' is not one of the eight: '**Idle** for the trilemma; **catch-all with no gauge** for the wider "you can't tell" claim.' | turned_own_test is N because this is the document testing itself, not the reader turning a test back on it: 'Bostrom does the "build the best rival" test on this part himself: he distinguishes the bland principle from the stronger self-sampling assumption behind the Doomsday argument... That is a genuine, self-administered test, and it survives it.'
